game_identity.player_fantasy: Be the last maintenance runner carrying unstable charge from a central core to failing relays fast enough to keep the network alive.
game_identity.central_interaction: Route, recharge, carry, and transfer charge between a central core and four decaying relay beacons.

playable_loop: Move -> recharge at core -> choose upper/lower passage -> carry charge -> read changing relay urgency -> choose which relay to service -> touch beacon to transfer -> manage decay -> stabilize all four or black out -> retry

controls.move: WASD, arrow keys, or standard-mapped gamepad left stick / D-pad
controls.restart: R, Restart button, or standard-mapped gamepad Start

technology_stack: Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript Canvas; local/offline browser; no dependencies
current_milestone: Route-Urgency Tradeoff Slice: prove that route cost and live relay urgency can compete inside one service decision rather than remaining separately proven facts. On one exact accepted composition, find a normal-run snapshot with at least two plausible reachable relay choices where one has a meaningful route-cost advantage and another has a meaningful live-urgency advantage, with no option trivially dominating both dimensions. Execute controlled continuations and measure the network consequence/trade using route time, runner-charge spend, offline exposure, preserved online count, recovery burden, or completion margin. Expose both route shape and relay state in the accepted browser composition without hidden debug data. Test the existing geometry/decay/readability model before adding hazards, relay classes, resources, scoring, or another primary verb. Human/fresh-player PLAYTESTED evidence remains required before claims that the tradeoff is perceived, understandable, fair, tense, balanced, or fun.
known_failures: Accepted main still has no full normal-input WON session reported PLAYTESTED by a genuine human/fresh player; this remains a validation gap, not an autonomous progression gate.
Accepted main still has no full normal-input BLACKOUT session reported PLAYTESTED by a genuine human/fresh player; this remains a validation gap, not an autonomous progression gate.

Accepted main exposes live relay percentages and contextual state/transfer cues, but no genuine fresh-player evidence shows that a human interprets relay urgency or route-versus-urgency tradeoffs correctly.

The current accepted evidence proves route consequence and live-state consequence separately; it has not yet proven one same-snapshot decision where route advantage and urgency advantage oppose each other without one choice dominating both dimensions.

Literal packaged file:// or localhost launch remains blocked in some specialist environments despite structural wiring tests; accepted route/readability inspection used exact repository runtime/presentation bytes in real Chromium with inlining only to bypass that navigation restriction.
Standard-mapped gamepad behavior is covered by simulated Gamepad API regression evidence, but physical gamepad hardware and cross-browser Gamepad API behavior remain unverified.
build_run_instructions: Open index.html in a modern desktop browser, or run python -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000.

evidence_status.triage_slice: COMPLETED / preserved on Integration PR #33 composition. The first loop centers on transporting charge between a core and independently decaying relays.
Autonomous Loop Closure Evidence is satisfied on accepted main by machine-executed WON, BLACKOUT, and retry plus real Chromium VISUALLY INSPECTED terminal/restart output.
Human/fresh-player PLAYTESTED evidence remains important but is not an autonomous progression gate; later human evidence may still trigger repair or direction changes.
